title: Dynamic Stabilisers

positions.as_written: Examine hip abductor strength and single leg control when the patella is unstable, because the groove's position is set above the knee.
Expect the oblique fibres to waste first and recover last, and record thigh circumference rather than relying on inspection.
Consider the lateral side as well as the medial, since the imbalance can come from either.
Treat dynamic stabilisation as the modifiable part of patellar stability.
Treat dynamic stabilisation as setting the position from which the passive restraints are loaded.
Assess the hip and the trunk before concluding that a patellar problem is local.
Expect rehabilitation to help where the passive anatomy is near normal and to help less where it is not, and say which case a patient is in.
Consider the coupling between the oblique fibres and a reconstructed ligament when planning rehabilitation after reconstruction.
Avoid describing selective strengthening of the oblique fibres as achievable in isolation.
